<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Beleg Tâl" /></noinclude>{{Verse|2|12}} And the gold of that land {{smaller|is}} good: There {{smaller|is}} Bdellium and the Onix ſtone.

{{Verse|2|13}} And the name of the ſecond riuer {{smaller|is}} Gihon: the ſame {{smaller|is it}} that compaſſeth the whole land of †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=† ''Heb. Cuſh.''}} Ethiopia.

{{Verse|2|14}} And the name of the third riuer {{smaller|is}} Hiddekel: that {{smaller|is it}} which goeth ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=ǁ''Or, Eastward to Aſſyria.''}} toward the Eaſt of Aſſyria: and the fourth riuer {{smaller|is}} Euphrates.

{{Verse|2|15}} And the LORD God tooke ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=ǁ''Or, Adam.''}} the man, and put him into the garden of Eden, to dreſſe it, and to keepe it.

{{Verse|2|16}} And the LORD God commanded the man, ſaying, Of euery tree of the garden thou mayeſt †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=† ''Hebr. eating thou ſhalt eate.''}} freely eate.

{{Verse|2|17}} But of the tree of the knowledge of good and euill, thou ſhalt not eate of it: for in the day that thou eateſt thereof, thou ſhalt †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=† ''Hebr. dying thou ſhalt die.''}} ſurely die.

{{Verse|2|18}} ¶ And the LORD God ſaid, It {{smaller|is}} not good that the man ſhould be alone: I will make him *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=* Ecclus. 17. 5.}} an helpe †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=† ''Hebr. as before him.''}} meet for him.

{{Verse|2|19}} And out of ye ground the LORD God formed euery beaſt of the field, and euery foule of the aire, and brought {{smaller|them}} vnto ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=ǁ''Or, the man.''}} Adam, to ſee what he would call them: and whatſoeuer Adam called euery liuing creature, that {{smaller|was}} the name thereof.

{{Verse|2|20}} And Adam †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=† ''Hebr. called.''}} gaue names to all
cattell, and to the foule of the aire, and to euery beaſt of the fielde: but for Adam there was not found an helpe meete for him.

{{Verse|2|21}} And the LORD God cauſed a deepe ſleepe to fall vpon Adam, and hee ſlept; and he tooke one of his ribs, and cloſed vp the fleſh in ſtead thereof.

{{Verse|2|22}} And the rib which the LORD God had taken from man, †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=† ''Hebr. builded.''}} made hee a woman, ⁊ brought her vnto the man.

{{Verse|2|23}} And Adam ſaid, This {{smaller|is}} now bone of my bones, and fleſh of my fleſh: ſhe ſhalbe called woman, becauſe ſhee was *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=* 1. Corin. 11. 8.}} taken out of man.

{{Verse|2|24}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=* Matt. 19. 5. mar. 10. 7. 1. corin. 6. 16. ephe. 5. 31.}} Therefore ſhall a man leaue his father and his mother, and ſhall cleaue vnto his wife: and they ſhalbe one fleſh.

{{Verse|2|25}} And they were both naked, the man ⁊ his wife, and were not aſhamed.

==={{Chapter|3|CHAP. III.}}===

{{smaller block|[[#3:1|1]] The ſerpent deceiueth Eue. [[#3:6|6]] Mans ſhamefull fall. [[#3:9|9]] God arraigneth them. [[#3:14|14]] The ſerpent is curſed. [[#3:15|15]] The promiſed Seed. [[#3:16|16]] The puniſhment of Mankind. [[#3:21|21]] Their firſt clothing. [[#3:22|22]] Their caſting out of Paradiſe.}}

{{Verse|3|1|notext=}} {{dropinitial|N|image=King James Bible (1611) page A2r (N).xcf|imgsize=100px}}Ow the ſerpent was more ſubtill then any beaſt of the field, which the LORD God had made, and he ſaid vnto the woman, †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=† ''Heb. Yea, becauſe, &c.''}} Yea, hath God ſaid, Ye ſhall not eat of euery tree of the garden?

{{Verse|3|2}} And the woman ſaid vnto the ſerpent, Wee may eate of the fruite of the trees of the garden:

{{Verse|3|3}} But of the fruit of the tree, which {{smaller|is}} in the midſt of the garden, God hath ſaid, Ye ſhal not eate of it, neither ſhall ye touch it, leſt ye die.

{{Verse|3|4}} And the Serpent ſaid vnto the woman, Ye ſhall not *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=* 2. Cor. 11 3. 1. tim. 2. 14.}} ſurely die.

{{Verse|3|5}} For God doeth know, that in the day ye eate thereof, then your eyes ſhalbee opened: and yee ſhall bee as Gods, knowing good and euill.

{{Verse|3|6}} And when the woman ſaw, that the tree {{smaller|was}} good for food, and that it {{smaller|was}} †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=† ''Heb. a deſire.''}} pleaſant to the eyes, and a tree to be deſired to make one wiſe, ſhe tooke of the fruit thereof, *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=* Ecclus. 25 26. 1. tim. 2. 14.}} and did eate, and gaue alſo vnto her huſband with her, and hee did eate.

{{Verse|3|7}} And the eyes of them both were opened, ⁊ they knew that they {{smaller|were}} naked, and they ſewed figge leaues together, and made themſelues ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=ǁ''Or, things to gird about.''}} aprons.

{{Verse|3|8}} And they heard the voyce of the LORD God, walking in the garden in the †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=† ''Heb. wind.''}} coole of the day: and Adam and his wife hid themſelues from the preſence of the LORD God, amongſt the trees of the garden.

{{Verse|3|9}} And the LORD God called vnto Adam, and ſaid vnto him, Where {{smaller|art}} thou?

{{Verse|3|10}} And he ſaid, I heard thy voice in the garden: and I was afraid, becauſe I {{smaller|was}} naked, and I hid my ſelfe.

{{Verse|3|11}} And he ſaid, Who told thee, that thou {{smaller|waſt}} naked? Haſt thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee, that thou ſhouldeſt not eate?

{{Verse|3|12}} And the man ſaid, The woman whom thou gaueſt {{smaller|to be}} with mee, ſhee gaue me of the tree, and I did eate.

{{Verse|3|13}} And the LORD God ſaid vnto the woman, What {{smaller|is}} this {{smaller|that}} thou haſt done? And the woman ſaid, The Serpent beguiled me, and I did eate.

{{Verse|3|14}} And the LORD God ſaid vnto the Serpent, Becauſe thou haſt done this, thou {{smaller|art}} curſed aboue all cattel, and aboue euery beaſt of the field: vpon thy belly ſhalt thou goe, and duſt ſhalt thou<noinclude></noinclude>
